title: CrowdStrike to Buy Zscaler for $43.9 Billion as AI Supercharges Cyberattacks
yt_title: CrowdStrike Buys Zscaler for $43.9 Billion: A New Cybersecurity Giant
yt_description:
CrowdStrike is acquiring Zscaler in an all-stock deal worth about $43.9 billion. Each Zscaler share becomes 1.135 CrowdStrike shares (about $260, a 34% premium), the combined company brings roughly $10 billion in annual recurring revenue, and CrowdStrike moves into network security as AI speeds up cyberattacks. Zscaler jumped 17% while CrowdStrike slid more than 8% before the open; the deal still needs regulatory and shareholder approval.

script: Welcome to IT News, AI News! The cybersecurity world just got a brand new giant. CrowdStrike is buying Zscaler, in an all stock deal worth about forty three point nine billion dollars. That's not a typo. Almost forty four billion dollars, paid entirely in shares. Every Zscaler share becomes one point one three five CrowdStrike shares. That works out to about two hundred sixty dollars a share, a thirty four percent premium. Why now? Because AI is turbocharging cyberattacks, and attackers find holes faster than ever. CrowdStrike guards the endpoint. Your laptops, your servers, your devices. Zscaler guards the network, with its zero trust cloud platform. Put them together, and CrowdStrike walks into network security, which it calls the single largest market in the field. The two companies already share about two thousand customers. Awkward family dinner? Not anymore. Combined, they bring roughly ten billion dollars in yearly recurring revenue. CrowdStrike is aiming for about one billion dollars in yearly synergies within thirty months. Zscaler boss Jay Chaudhry will run the Zscaler business, and join CrowdStrike's board. Wall Street was split. Zscaler jumped seventeen percent, while CrowdStrike slid more than eight percent before the open. Analysts say the combo can fight Palo Alto Networks harder. But regulators still have to sign off, with closing expected around this time next year. Read the full story on itnewsainews dot xpigeon dot net. See you next time!
